sample_unit: patients (3 test sets of 117 Barrett's patients each)
models_evaluated: computer aided detection deep learning system for Barrett's neoplasia

links.outcome: AI performance on images with real-world quality variation and artefacts
links.effect: Trained on high-quality data, AUC fell from 83% (high quality) to 80% (moderate) and 71% (low); sensitivity fell from 85% to 62% and 47%.
links.quote: AUC and sensitivity were significantly lower with 80% (p < 0.001) and 62% (p = 0.002) on the moderate-quality and 71% (p > 0.001) and 47% (p = 0.002) on the low-quality test set.

links.outcome: Performance drop when moving from expert-image development data to heterogeneous community-like imaging
links.effect: Sensitivity dropped from 85% on high-quality images to 62% on moderate-quality and 47% on low-quality test sets; AUC fell from 83% to 71%.
links.quote: Endoscopic deep learning systems trained solely on high-quality images may not perform well when exposed to heterogeneous imagery, as found in routine practice.

unlisted_practices: Domain-specific pretraining to improve robustness to image quality heterogeneity
Architectural optimization to improve robustness to data heterogeneity
Including more diverse-quality training data to mitigate performance loss

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates performance degradation caused by real-world image heterogeneity and assesses concrete mitigation strategies (diverse training data, domain-specific pretraining) to address clinical transferability and robustness.

primary.practice: robustness training with heterogeneous data and domain pretraining
